In a regulated market, there are people who possess the authority to decree, for instance, who may or may not take part. Creating one core code for different OS and devices makes no sense. It sound nice on power point slides, but the practicality makes it hard to maintain.

  • Your core code becomes incredibly complex (exponentially). You must take into account different screen sizes, different devices and different OS. One bug fixed for one device introduces another bug for all other OS.
  • Your developer must know every single device and OS. Which makes it a rare breed. I guarantee you that he will develop for one device he knows best and then shoehorn it to the other OS and makes it suck.
  • Testing becomes exponentially more complex. You need to test on every single OS and device out there.
  • In a perfect world creating core code could become UI independent. But in my experience it never does. Small variations in UI behavior forces you to redesign your core code.

And the hard reality is that designing and maintaining 3 different apps as 3 separate projects using the best tools for that device and OS is the biggest chance of success and a way faster release cycle. If I introduce a bug in one OS version then I don't break the app in all other OS versions. And you can have 3 developers all focused on streamlining for that specific OS to have the best user experience.
